Loading Subpackages

In some cases, developers need to divide a Mini Program into different packages and pack the packages into different subpackages during construction. Users can load the subpackages as required.

During constructing subpackages of a Mini Program, one or more subpackages are generated. Each Mini Program which uses the subpackages must contain a main package. The main package stores the default startup page or tabBar page and common resources or JavaScript scripts, required by all packages. Packages are divided based on the developer's configuration.

When a Mini Program is started, the main package is downloaded and the page in the main package is displayed by default. When a user accesses a page in a subpackage, the client downloads the corresponding subpackage and displays the page after the download is complete. Dividing packages for a Mini Program can optimize the download time for the first startup of the Mini Program and facilitate decoupling and collaboration when multiple teams jointly develop a Mini Program.

Use Subpackages

Configuration Method

Assume that the directory structure of a Mini Program that supports package dividing is as follows:

├── app.js
├── app.json
├── app.mass
├── packageA
│   └── pages
│       ├── apple
│       └── banana
├── packageB
│   └── pages
│       ├── dog
│       └── cat
├── pages
│   ├── index
│   └── logs
└── utils

Developers declare the project subpackage structure using the subPackages field of the app.json file.

{
  "pages": ["pages/index", "pages/logs"],
  "subPackages": [
    {
      "root": "packageA",
      "pages": ["pages/apple", "pages/banana"]
    },
    {
      "root": "packageB",
      "pages": ["pages/cat", "pages/dog"]
    }
  ]
}

In subPackages, the configuration attributes of each subpackage are as follows:

Field Type Description
root String Subpackage root directory.
pages Array Subpackage page directory.

Principles of Packaging

  • After subPackages is used to declare, packages are packed according to the directories specified by subPackages. The subpackages in other directories are packed into the main package.
  • A main package can also have its own pages (that is, the outermost pages field).
  • The root directory of subPackages cannot be a sub-directory of another subPackages.
  • The tabBar page must be contained in the main package.

Principles of Referencing

  • packageA cannot require the JavaScript files of packageB, but can require the JavaScript files in the main package and its own package.
  • packageA cannot import the template of packageB, but can import the template of the main package and its own package.
  • packageA cannot use the resources of packageB, but can use the resources of the main package and its own package.
